title: Andrew Rannells Recalls Receiving a Date Invitation From Kevin Spacey
excerpt:
The Broadway actor described an unexpected backstage encounter during The Book of Mormon.
He says a handwritten invitation arrived later, but he never replied.
body_md:
Andrew Rannells has shared a previously untold personal story about an encounter with Kevin Spacey during his time starring in the Broadway musical The Book of Mormon. Speaking on The Downside podcast, Rannells recalled receiving a handwritten letter from Spacey asking him on a date after the two met backstage.

Rannells originated the role of Elder Price when the musical opened in 2011 and continued in the production until June 2012. His performance earned a Tony Award nomination for leading actor in a musical, placing him at the center of a highly successful Broadway run.

According to Rannells, Spacey attended a performance and subsequently appeared in his dressing room area along with Goldie Hawn and director Joel Schumacher. Rannells described the backstage visit as unexpected, explaining that celebrity guests were sometimes brought into dressing rooms without advance notice while performers were changing after a show.

Rannells recalled that Spacey touched his neck during the encounter. He also said Schumacher, whom he knew well, warned him to keep his distance. Approximately a week later, according to Rannells, a handwritten letter arrived at the theater asking him on a date. He said he did not respond.

The account is Rannells' recollection of events and should not be treated as an independently established account of every interaction. It also predates the public allegations against Spacey that emerged in 2017.

Those later allegations have been the subject of separate legal proceedings. In a 2022 New York civil trial brought by Anthony Rapp, a jury found Spacey not liable. Spacey also reached a settlement in 2026 with three men who had brought civil claims in London, avoiding a scheduled trial. Those legal outcomes should not be conflated with Rannells' newly shared anecdote.

The interview adds a personal Broadway-era recollection to the public conversation around the actors, while keeping the distinction between one person's account and adjudicated legal findings important.
